result.topic_en: A draft outline of articles 6–17 of Riemann's dissertation on complex functions, covering conformal mapping, the connectivity of surfaces, the Green/divergence integral theorem, harmonic functions, discontinuities, and the minimum principle (Dirichlet principle) for representing a given complex quantity as a function of z.

items.english: 17. A variable complex quantity α+βi, arbitrarily given for the points of T, can always, and in only one way, be converted into a function of z, provided the integral over the whole surface is finite. This is done by adding a variable complex quantity that is purely imaginary on the boundary, satisfies certain continuity conditions, and whose imaginary part is to take a given value at one point.
